symptoms: Trauma patient: Unresponsive, not breathing or only gasping, no pulse.
If ultrasound available and no cardiac wall motion: consider not starting resuscitation.

management_steps.details: Ensure scene safe, don PPE. Manual C-spine alignment throughout. Call for assistance and activate trauma team.

H - Haemorrhage Control: Apply tourniquets / direct pressure, bind pelvis, straighten/stabilise long bone fractures, IV/IO access above pelvis and provide 20ml/kg warmed crystalloids (or whole blood/massive transfusion protocol/PRCs & FFP). O - Oxygenation and Ventilation: Place advanced airway (ETT/SGA), ventilate with 100% O2 at min 15L/min flowrate. T - Tension Pneumothorax: Consider empiric bilateral chest decompression (5th IC space anterior axillary line; finger thoracostomy preferred). T - Tamponade: Diagnose with Ultrasound, consider thoracotomy or pericardial window.
If ROSC: Follow post cardiac arrest algorithm, consider urgent surgical intervention and administration of TxA. If no ROSC: Consider termination of efforts.

warnings: Prioritise H-O-T-T interventions simultaneously using a multi-member team.
